issues.problem: The English title is truncated: it drops the second half of the Chinese title, 「一个不肯白送的人」 (the man who refused a free throwaway / refused to give it away for nothing). The English covers only 'Turning Back at the Yimen Gate: The Year Handan Was Besieged'.
issues.suggestion: Append the missing element, e.g. 'Turning Back at the Yimen Gate: The Year Handan Was Besieged, and the Man Who Would Not Give It Away Free'.

issues.problem: The English adds facts not present in the Chinese: 'The king set down the game and reached for his ministers. Lord Xinling stopped him' and 'the game resumed' (the Chinese only says beacon fires alarmed the border and the lord said it was the Zhao king hunting, later confirmed). The English also expands '门客中有人能得赵王阴事' into 'and that whatever the Zhao king did, the man reported back to him'.
issues.suggestion: Delete 'The king set down the game and reached for his ministers. Lord Xinling stopped him:' and 'and the game resumed', and reduce the last clause to 'a man who could ferret out the king of Zhao's private business' — or add the same details to the Chinese.

issues.problem: English adds small details absent from the Chinese: identifying the Yimen as 'the eastern gate of Daliang', 'called on him', 'and when everyone was seated', 'with his carriage and escort', and interpreting Hou Ying's not yielding the seat as 'testing his host'.
issues.suggestion: Trim these additions (e.g. drop '— testing his host', 'and when everyone was seated') or add the same details to the Chinese.

issues.problem: English adds the question 'Had he fallen short somewhere?' and the phrase 'reasoning that', which the Chinese sentence does not contain (it ends at '对方竟无一言半辞相送').
issues.suggestion: Remove 'Had he fallen short somewhere?' (and optionally 'reasoning that'), or add the equivalent question to the Chinese.

issues.problem: English adds 'and from the king on down no one could get it for her' to the story of Lady Ruji's father's murder, which the Chinese does not state; and renders 「顧未有路耳」 as 'she had no way to repay him' where the Chinese says only that she had no avenue to act.
issues.suggestion: Drop 'and from the king on down no one could get it for her', and render the quote as 'she had no way to do it' / 'no avenue had opened for her'.

overall: The English matches the Chinese closely in facts, quotes, dates and hedges throughout, with one truncated title and a few small narrative additions in the Hou Ying and Lady Ruji passages that should be trimmed or mirrored.
